description: Remove builtin-workflow knowledge from generic C# code: Definition-sourced metric stage order, unconditional parent-context attachment, three-layer variable model, and workflow-authored rebase recovery.

tasks.title: Source quality metric stage set and order from the Definition
tasks.description: Delete the `QualityStageOrder` constant from `IssueMetricsQuerier`. Thread the Definition-sourced stage order (via `ResolveProjectStageOrderAsync`) into `BuildWindow`, filtering to only entered stages and preserving Definition order with non-Definition observed stages appended after. Update accumulator/window unit tests and add a spec test for custom-stage-name metrics.
acceptanceCriteria: `QualityStageOrder` constant does not exist anywhere in the codebase.
Quality windows for custom profiles contain only stages from the bound Definition, in Definition order, with no entered=0 phantom rows for builtin stage names.
Quality windows for builtin profiles produce the identical stage list, entered counts, and rework rates as before this change.
Cross-profile windows list each distinct stage id once, with Definition-ordered stages first and remaining observed stages appended after.
Spec test covers a custom-stage Run appearing in Definition order without ghost rows, and builtin-profile metric parity.
`npm test` passes.
tasks.output: Updated `IssueMetricsQuerier.cs` with Definition-sourced stage ordering and passing metric tests.
tasks.notes: Mirror the stage-duration path's `ResolveProjectStageOrderAsync` + orderedStages pattern. The project default profile's Definition provides the primary ordering.

tasks.title: Attach parent issue context unconditionally for workflow task dispatches
tasks.description: Remove the `stage == "plan" && uses == "mohist/opencode"` guard from `ToWorkDispatchResponseAsync`. Attach parent issue context for all workflow-owned task dispatches (`OwnerKind == Workflow`, `WorkType == Task`) with a valid projectId and issueNumber. Update `RunnerPollParentContextMapperSpecs` to reflect unconditional attachment.
acceptanceCriteria: `ToWorkDispatchResponseAsync` contains no comparison of `Stage` or `Uses` against the literals `plan` or `mohist/opencode`.
Parent issue context is attached for all workflow task dispatches carrying a valid issue, including tasks in non-plan stages and non-opencode actions.
Parent context remains null for issues without a parent, for checks dispatches, and for agent-job dispatches.
`RunnerPollParentContextMapperSpecs` updated to verify unconditional attachment for workflow tasks and null for non-workflow or non-task dispatches.
`npm test` passes.
tasks.output: Updated `RunnerRoutes.cs` with unconditional parent-context attachment and passing dispatch mapper tests.
tasks.notes: The `resolveParentIssueContext` callback returns null for parentless issues, so nothing is attached in that case. `WorkDispatch` shape is unchanged.

tasks.title: Collapse variable model to three layers and remove the defaults machinery
tasks.description: Remove `DefaultVars`/`DefaultStages` from `VariableBundle`, the `EnsureArchiveDefaultAsync` seed path, the clear-on-explicit-write protocol, and the `DefaultVariables` persistence column. Simplify `MergeRunScopedVariables` to `MergeAll(project, issue, run)`. Add an EF Core migration to drop the column. Add a runner spec test confirming archive absent-hint behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: `VariableBundle` record has only `Vars` and `Stages` parameters; `DefaultVars`, `DefaultStages`, `HasDefaultContent`, `ClearDefaultsCoveredByExplicit`, and all stripping/intersection helpers do not exist.
No reference to `EnsureArchiveDefaultAsync`, `ArchiveDefaultKey`, `GetDefaultVariablesAsync`, `BuildArchiveDefaultElement`, `HasArchiveKey`, or `DefaultVariables` remains in server code.
`WorkflowGrain` startup does not call any archive-default seeding method.

EF Core migration drops the `DefaultVariables` column from `WorkflowRunProfiles`; `WorkflowRunProfileRow` has no `DefaultVariables` property and `MohistDbContext` has no `DefaultVariables` configuration.
Run startup produces effective variables with no `archive` key unless explicitly declared by a Project, Issue, or Run variable.
Runner `mohist/archive-change` spec test covers absent-hint behavior: the action computes a fresh dated destination and moves the change directory.
All former `DefaultVars`/`DefaultStages` unit and spec tests are updated or removed; no dead test code remains.
`npm test` passes (server); `npm run typecheck` and `npm run test:run` pass (runner).
tasks.output: Slimmed `VariableBundle`, removed defaults machinery, dropped persistence column with migration, and passing server + runner tests.
tasks.notes: AGENTS.md states no version compat is needed; Orleans serializer ID shifts are acceptable. Old `Variables` JSON may contain stale `DefaultVars`/`DefaultStages` keys — System.Text.Json ignores unmapped members by default.

tasks.title: Author rebase recovery in workflow content via top-level recoveries key
tasks.description: Add a top-level `recoveries` key to the workflow YAML schema, parsed into `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, RecoveryDefinition>` on `WorkflowDefinition`. Declare a `rebase-conflicts` template in both builtin YAMLs. Rewrite the rebase route to source recovery from the profile definition. Delete `BuildRebaseRecovery()`. Update `design/workflow/recovery.md` with the one-mechanism decision and the `recoveries` key documentation.
acceptanceCriteria: `WorkflowDefinitionParser` accepts and parses a top-level `recoveries` mapping; `WorkflowDefinition` carries a `Recoveries` dictionary.
`WorkflowYamlSerializer` round-trips the `recoveries` section.
Both builtin YAMLs declare a `rebase-conflicts` recovery template containing the `mohist/opencode` conflict-resolution task with `budget: 2` and the `error.code=conflict` handler.
`IssueRoutes.Helpers` no longer contains `BuildRebaseRecovery` or constructs any `RecoveryDefinition`, `RecoveryHandlerDefinition`, or `TaskDefinition`.
The rebase route resolves the run's bound profile and reads `definition.Recoveries["rebase-conflicts"]` for the recovery definition.
`mo issue rebase` produces the same recovery task with the same budget, handler ordering, prompt reference, and `mohist/opencode` handler as before.

`design/workflow/recovery.md` documents that API-triggered one-shot injection and Profile-driven recovery are one mechanism, and that the `recoveries` top-level key is the home for named recovery templates.
`npm test` passes (server); `npm run typecheck` and `npm run test:run` pass (runner).
tasks.output: Parser/model/serializer support for `recoveries`, updated builtin YAMLs, rewritten rebase route, updated `recovery.md`, and passing tests.
tasks.notes: `BuildRebaseTaskWith(baseBranch)` stays — it constructs runtime input with a dynamic baseBranch, not workflow-definition structure. The `recoveries` parser reuses the existing `BuildRecovery` logic.
